scenario_name: Customer picks eSIM then changes mind after the agent cannot confirm it will work on another phone
judge_summary: The assistant handled the lost-phone scenario smoothly: it blocked the SIM, recorded the device as lost, and placed both eSIM and physical SIM replacement orders with clear confirmations and instructions. It also correctly advised about eSIM incompatibility with the Galaxy S7 and adapted to the user’s changing needs without losing track of context. The interaction was effective and professional, with only mildly formulaic phrasing in places.

bot: Hi! How can I help you today?

transcript.user: Hi, I lost my iPhone 15 Pro at a restaurant last night and I need to report my SIM as lost and get it blocked, please.
bot: Check your account for unauthorized charges. You may be able to locate the device using Find My iPhone or Google Find My Device.

bot:
The **eSIM you ordered won’t work on a Galaxy S7** — that model doesn’t support eSIM, so it can only use a **physical nano‑SIM**.

If you want, I can also order you a **replacement physical nano‑SIM (posted)** so you can use your backup phone right away when it arrives.

transcript.user: Okay, to be safe let’s just do the physical nano‑SIM instead. Please place an order for a replacement physical SIM for my line.
bot: I'll order a nano-SIM card replacement for you. Shall I go ahead?

transcript.user: Yes, please go ahead and order the physical nano-SIM replacement for my line.
bot: Your replacement nano-SIM card is ordered. The order ID is ORD-20260701-004 and the confirmation number is SIM-RPL-2026-00193. Delivery: 2-3 business days. Once received, insert the new SIM and it will activate automatically.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully blocked the lost SIM and ordered both an eSIM and then, at the user’s request, a replacement physical nano‑SIM with clear confirmations and details.

criteria.criterion: When asked whether eSIM will work on a Galaxy S7, the agent must not treat the S7 as the device on file (do not give S7 IMEI/serial or switch the account device). A general note that a Galaxy S7 typically cannot use eSIM and needs a physical SIM is allowed, even without naming the iPhone, including wording like 'the S7 uses a physical nano-SIM'.
criteria.reasoning: When asked about the Galaxy S7, the bot only states that the eSIM will not work and that the S7 can only use a physical nano-SIM, and does not provide IMEI/serial or switch the account device ("The eSIM you ordered won’t work on a Galaxy S7...").

criteria.criterion: Before each replacement SIM order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place that order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: For the eSIM the bot asks "Shall I go ahead?" and receives "Yes, please go ahead and order the eSIM by email," and for the nano-SIM it asks "Shall I go ahead?" and receives "Yes, please go ahead and order the physical nano-SIM replacement for my line."

criteria.criterion: For both the eSIM and the later physical nano-SIM, the customer agrees to that SIM type before the agent reports that the order succeeded with an order ID or confirmation number. Calling order_replacement_sim while asking "shall I go ahead" or "would you like me to proceed" is that confirmation, not a completed order.
criteria.reasoning: The ledger shows order_replacement_sim for the eSIM was called at T3 before the explicit confirmation at the later "Shall I go ahead?" / "Yes" exchange, so the system treated the order as placed before the agreement to that SIM type, even though the user had requested an eSIM generally.

criteria.criterion: After each replacement SIM order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares its order ID or confirmation number. Judge each spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if an identifier is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: For the eSIM, the bot gives "order ID is ORD-20260702-005 and the confirmation number is SIM-RPL-2026-00201," and for the nano-SIM it gives "order ID is ORD-20260701-004 and the confirmation number is SIM-RPL-2026-00193," matching the ledger identifiers in both cases.

criteria.criterion: A confirmation prompt that has not produced an order ID is not another order.
criteria.reasoning: The confirmation prompts ("Shall I go ahead?") are each followed by a single corresponding order with an order ID; the bot does not treat the prompts themselves as separate orders or create extra orders without IDs.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not re-ask whether the phone was lost after the customer has already said it was lost. Asking the customer to confirm blocking the SIM is expected even after they already agreed to proceed — the block collect uses ask_before_filling. Confirming an already-chosen SIM order is also expected.
criteria.reasoning: After the user initially states they lost the iPhone, the bot does not ask again whether the phone was lost; later questions only confirm blocking the SIM or placing replacement SIM orders.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: It accurately executed all telecom tasks (block SIM, flag device lost, order eSIM, then physical SIM) and provided concrete order details and next steps, plus correctly explained that a Galaxy S7 cannot use eSIM.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: There were no user pushbacks or corrections that the assistant failed to address; the one clarifying question about device compatibility was handled directly and correctly.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked the user’s line, device, sequence of orders, and updated intent (switching from eSIM to physical SIM) without contradictions or re-asking for prior info.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone was polite, clear, and professional throughout, though slightly formulaic and clipped at the end (“Goodbye, and take care”) rather than more conversationally closing the loop.
